reconstructed_theorem_text: Let Omega be a measurable space with measure mu, F a filtration on nonnegative time, and J a finite coordinate type with decidable equality. Let B:[0,infinity) x Omega -> R^J be a standard Brownian motion with F: zero at time zero for every sample, jointly independent increments over finite disjoint half-open intervals, centered Gaussian increment projections with variance (t-s)*||ell||^2, almost-sure continuous paths, strong F-adaptedness, and increment independence from F_s for s<=t. Fix T>=0. For each n in N, i=0,...,2^n-1 and j in J, let c_{n,i,j}:Omega->R be strongly measurable for F_{i*T/2^n}, belong to L4(mu), and satisfy integral c_{n,i,j}^4 dmu<=C, for one real constant C uniform over n,i,j. Write t_i^n=i*T/2^n and define E_n(omega)=sum_i [ (sum_j c_{n,i,j}(omega)*(B_j(t_{i+1}^n,omega)-B_j(t_i^n,omega)))^2 -(sum_j c_{n,i,j}(omega)^2)*(t_{i+1}^n-t_i^n) ]. Then E_n belongs to L2(mu) for every n, and integral E_n^2 dmu tends to zero as n tends to infinity. No positive-horizon or usual-conditions assumption, and no separate finite-measure instance, appears in this statement.
objects: Omega,mu,F,finite J, vector standard Brownian B, horizon T, triangular array c indexed by n,dyadic cell i,coordinate j, bound C, error E_n.
domains: Time NNReal; T>=0; n natural; i in Fin(2^n); coefficients/error real; J finite with decidable equality.
quantifiers: For every admissible space and B, every T and coefficient array satisfying left-endpoint measurability and L4, every real C bounding all fourth moments, the two conclusions hold.
assumptions: B standard Brownian with F; each coefficient strongly F_{t_i^n}-measurable; each coefficient in L4(mu); integral fourth power<=C uniformly in n,i,j.
conclusion: Every E_n is in L2(mu), and its squared L2 integral tends to zero.
scopes: All dyadic levels on fixed [0,T]; ordinary real convergence of second moments as n->infinity, hence specified mean-square statement; no almost-sure convergence or rate asserted.
constant_dependencies: The same C serves every level,cell,coordinate; it may depend on the whole coefficient family and underlying data. No rate constant is concluded.
